messages:
Alex: heads-up — noticed a tail-latency and throughput regression on the mixed-4 rollout last night. telemetry shows memory surges + kernel reloads on ~6% of nodes.
Mira: saw this too, reproducible on canary-3. pattern looks like a sequence: large-context request -> kernel fallback -> KV eviction burst -> batch window cutting leads to extra kernel churn. :thinking:
Sam: dumped a runtime profile and heap map. kernel selector churn spikes aligned with batching boundaries. attaching quick log excerpt.
Sam: ```
[03:12:46.112] kernel_select: try nf4_fast
[03:12:46.118] kernel_select: fallback fp4_safe (quant_mismatch)
[03:12:46.119] kv_cache: async_eviction_start batch_id=4421
[03:12:46.121] batching: coalesce_cutoff fired (2ms)
[03:12:46.122] kernel_load: realloc_map failed -> fallthrough int8_slowpath
```
Jen: question — is this triggered by the batching heuristics (coalesce window) or by the calibration path swapping kernels?
Alex: both. our selector priority list + 2ms coalesce looks like a perfect storm: when a long-context request arrives it prefers nf4_fast, but a memory-layout change (fp4_safe) causes mmap remap and eviction. eviction frees slabs mid-batch which forces kernel binaries to be reloaded for the next micro-batches.
Mira: numbers from node-7a: baseline 1,200 tok/s -> 650 tok/s during spike. p95 from ~180ms -> ~520ms. RSS increased ~1.6GB.
Luis: I saw kernel binary remap errors in dmesg around the same time: 'remap_pages failed: -12'. that indicates address space fragmentation when we mmap new kernel blobs.
deploy-bot: deploy 1987-12-34 nf4-rollout-v2 started 03:00 UTC (canary: canary-1/2/3)
Luis: repro locally when feeding many long-context requests with jittered arrival times. reducing coalesce_ms to 0.5ms removes the cascade, but CPU sys goes up ~15%.
Alex: mitigation plan (short):
- pin batch sizes on critical routes (api-chat, api-complete) to reduce coalesce variability
- disable kernel hot-swap on dedicated NP nodes (force nf4 kernel load with conservative memory reservation)
- increase KV slab compaction interval to avoid large asynchronous eviction bursts
Mira: opened PR 4523 with a conservative selector tweak: prefer fixed-layout kernels for ctx_len > 2048 and add 5s hysteresis before allowing kernel swap. snippet: ```python
# runtime override
if ctx_len > 2048:
  selector.priority = [nf4_fixed, nf4_fast, fp4_safe, int8_fallback]
  selector.hysteresis_ms = 5000
```
Sam: created telemetry alert RT-1987 and added tracing to kernel_selection and kv_eviction spans. will run an extended canary overnight.
Jen: scheduling canary: will pin 3 nodes with the selector patch and coalesce_ms=0.5 on canary-3 at 04:15 UTC. will monitor p95 and RSS.
Mira: grabbing syscall traces and perf maps to see mmap patterns :eyes:
Luis: :thumbsup: i'll run heapprof and attach object hist after the first 30min run.
Alex: thanks. if p95 stays >300ms after the patch we roll back the rollout and run a postmortem. cc @Mira @Luis for follow-ups.
Jen: FYI rollback path prepared, documented in the runbook under 'nf4-rollout-rollback-2026' — will trigger if canary fails.
Mira: quick note — suspect this only shows up with mixed-precision churn + high variance of batch arrival; adding a per-request kernel-hint header might be a longer-term fix so clients with long contexts opt-in to fixed kernels.
Alex: agreed. add to backlog after stabilization. closing loop later today with findings and next steps. :white_check_mark:
